info.title: Tempera Payments API
info.description: A noncustodial payment-intent API. Atomic amounts are base-10 integer strings; decimal and floating-point money values are invalid. This contract is the producer source for tempera-sdk integration.

get.summary: Report that the process is reachable
get.description: A transport liveness probe. It performs no authorization, reads no tenant state, and proves nothing about durable storage or provider availability.

get.summary: List a tenant's payment intents by consumer reference, status, or creation window

parameters.name: referenceKind
parameters.description: Return only intents whose reference has this kind.

parameters.name: referenceId
parameters.description: Return only intents whose reference carries this consumer-owned identifier. Usable on its own, so a consumer that owns one identifier space does not have to send referenceKind.

parameters.name: referenceConsumer
parameters.description: Return only intents bound to this registered consumer service, for example `auth-hub`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only intents whose current projection has this lifecycle status.

parameters.name: createdAfter
parameters.description: Inclusive RFC3339 lower bound on intent creation time.

parameters.name: createdBefore
parameters.description: Exclusive RFC3339 upper bound on intent creation time.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Maximum intents to return. Out-of-range values are rejected rather than clamped.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: `nextPageToken` from the previous page, replayed with the identical filters. A token presented with a different filter set is rejected with reason `INVALID_PAGE_TOKEN`.

200.description: One page of the tenant's matching payment intents

get.summary: Read and cryptographically re-verify the canonical settlement receipt

post.summary: Create an idempotent hosted Stripe Checkout session for a fiat payment intent
Create a hosted/tokenizing card session with the selected configured acquirer
post.description: Routing occurs before provider tokenization. Tempera never accepts PAN or CVV in this API.

get.summary: Recover the centrally authenticated workspace and optional merchant
get.description: Uses the current Auth Hub organization claim. No caller-supplied tenant identifier or public mobile configuration chooses the returned workspace.

200.description: Authenticated workspace and current merchant, if created

get.summary: Read the merchant onboarding projection for one workspace

post.summary: Create the single US/USD merchant record for a workspace
post.description: Creates merchant onboarding state only. It does not prove incorporation, payment acceptance, or payout eligibility.

post.summary: Retrieve and store a fresh merchant eligibility observation
post.description: A provider observation is current only while its age is strictly less than 300 seconds. Refresh clears the prior eligibility projection before the provider call; a generation compare-and-set prevents a late response from an older refresh from overwriting a newer generation. An unavailable or malformed provider observation must not be treated as eligibility. A 429 carries the ErrorInfo reason MERCHANT_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED: the hourly per-merchant provider budget is exhausted.

post.summary: Create a short-lived Stripe-hosted merchant onboarding link
post.description: The URL is a bearer capability and must never be cached. If Stripe reports an expired link, request a new link with a new Idempotency-Key; do not replay an expired key. A 429 carries the ErrorInfo reason MERCHANT_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED: the hourly per-merchant provider budget is exhausted.

post.summary: Verify and durably deduplicate a Stripe webhook using its raw body
post.description: A Stripe-authored protocol receiver, not a Tempera resource method. It is authenticated by the Stripe-Signature HMAC over the exact raw body, never by a Tempera bearer token, and its request body is Stripe's own event envelope.

Issues one refund against the original provider settlement and commits it through the same correctness kernel the refund worker uses: the refund budget is reserved before the provider is contacted, the provider Refund object is retrieved authoritatively, and only then are the compensating journal and the signed operation receipt written. Answers 200 once the refund is economically committed and 202 with a pending refund while the provider outcome is not final or could not be observed; replaying the same tenantId, payment intent, idempotencyKey, and body returns the same refund and never refunds twice.

202.description: Refund accepted; the provider outcome is not final yet

get.summary: List the refunds of one payment intent
get.description: Refunds are returned newest first, ordered by createdAt.

post.summary: Create an idempotent hosted PayPal order for a fiat payment intent
post.description: Prepares one PayPal CAPTURE-intent order for an authorized iso4217 payment intent and returns the buyer approval URL. The order carries the Tempera payment intent id in custom_id and an idempotency-derived invoice_id, which are the bindings the settlement reconciler re-checks against PayPal's authoritative capture. Returns 503 when the PayPal rail is not configured.

post.summary: Verify and durably deduplicate a PayPal webhook using its raw body
post.description: A PayPal-authored protocol receiver, not a Tempera resource method. It is authenticated by PayPal's own verify-webhook-signature call over the exact raw body and the configured webhook id, never by a Tempera bearer token, and its request body is PayPal's own event envelope. The event is durable evidence and a reconciliation hint only: settlement is committed from an independently retrieved PayPal order or capture.

post.summary: Register a destination for signed payment events
post.description: Registers a URL this workspace controls as a destination for the signed `payment.settled` and `payment.refunded` events it subscribes to. The endpoint is delivered exactly the bytes that were signed, with the same `tempera-event-*` headers an internal consumer receives. A workspace may keep at most 10 active endpoints, and one URL may be active at most once.

get.summary: List the webhook endpoints of one workspace
get.description: Returns active and disabled endpoints, newest first. A disabled endpoint is kept so its delivery history stays readable.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: The nextPageToken of the previous page. Pages are keyset ordered newest first.

delete.summary: Stop delivering to a webhook endpoint
delete.description: Disables the endpoint. The row is never removed, so its delivery history stays coherent, and an event already fanned out to it is dead-lettered with `ENDPOINT_DISABLED` rather than posted to a withdrawn URL.

get.summary: List delivery attempts for one webhook endpoint
get.description: The delivery record of each event fanned out to this endpoint, newest first, so a brand can debug its own receiver.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: The nextPageToken of the previous page. Pages are keyset ordered newest first.

post.summary: Charge a saved payment method off-session for an authorized payment intent
post.description: Creates and confirms one provider charge against a payment method the intent's customer already saved, records the provider attempt, and returns. It settles nothing: the ledger journal, the signed receipt, and the `payment.settled` consumer event are produced by the same verified-webhook reconciliation path hosted checkout uses. A `requiresAction` charge needs the brand's own provider client-side authentication flow; Tempera does not perform it.

post.summary: Create a customer for one workspace
post.description: Creates Tempera's record of the brand's shopper. It performs no provider call: the provider customer is created lazily by the first setup session. When `externalId` is present the call is idempotent on `(tenantId, externalId)` and returns 200 for an identical replay, or 409 when the stored customer differs.

200.description: Equivalent idempotent replay of an existing externalId

get.summary: List customers of one workspace by an exact externalId or email
get.description: At least one of `externalId` or `email` is required and is matched exactly; this is a lookup, not a directory export.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Maximum customers to return. Defaults to 100, which is also the maximum.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A `nextPageToken` this API issued. Tokens are server-issued and are not caller-constructible.

post.summary: Create a provider-hosted session that saves a card for this customer
post.description: Creates or reuses this customer's provider customer, then a provider-hosted `setup` session bound to it. The shopper enters their card on the provider's page; Tempera never receives PAN or CVV. The saved payment method appears only after the verified provider webhook has been authoritatively re-read. Replays on `idempotencyKey`.

get.summary: List the payment methods saved for one customer
get.description: Returns provider handles and the non-sensitive display fields the provider publishes. Detached methods remain listed with status `detached`.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Maximum customers to return. Defaults to 100, which is also the maximum.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A `nextPageToken` this API issued. Tokens are server-issued and are not caller-constructible.

delete.description: Detaches the handle at the provider and records the method as `detached`. The row is never deleted, so a later charge attempt against it is refused rather than silently unrecognized. Detaching an already-detached method succeeds without calling the provider again.

scopes.payments:merchants:write: Create merchant onboarding records and links
scopes.payments:refunds:write: Issue refunds against settled payment intents
scopes.payments:refunds:read: Read refunds issued against payment intents
scopes.payments:webhooks:read: Read tenant-registered webhook endpoints and their delivery history
scopes.payments:webhooks:write: Register and remove tenant webhook endpoints for signed payment events
scopes.payments:customers:read: Read customers and their saved payment methods
scopes.payments:customers:write: Create customers, save payment methods, and charge them off-session

Status.description: The google.rpc.Status error envelope required of every Tempera API (AIP-193).

code.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body so the envelope is self-describing.

status.description: The canonical google.rpc.Code name, for example INVALID_ARGUMENT.

message.description: A developer-facing description that is safe to log and safe to show.

details.description: Structured error details. Present but empty when there are none.

requestId.description: The server-assigned request identifier, mirrored from the x-request-id response header.

AtomicAmount.description: Non-negative atomic integer. Never a decimal.

ReferenceKind.description: What the payment is for, in the consumer's vocabulary.

PaymentReference.description: Optional consumer binding. It routes signed settlement and refund events back to the named consumer service and never changes the economics of the intent.

id.description: Consumer-owned identifier such as an order ID, a credit top-up ID, or an invoice number.

consumer.description: Registered consumer service that receives signed `payment.settled` and `payment.refunded` events for this intent, for example `auth-hub`. Omitted means the event is recorded but not delivered to a service.

riskSubjectId.description: Pre-registered Tempera Risk subject ID for deterministic authorization.

customerId.description: Customer this intent is for. It must name a customer of the same tenant and never changes the economics of the intent.
Customer this intent is for. It must name a customer of the same tenant and never changes the economics of the intent.

clientPayload.description: Provider-issued payload passed to the selected provider's hosted/tokenizing frontend component. It contains no caller-supplied PAN/CVV fields.

MerchantCategory.description: The limited initial merchant categories; this is not a general marketplace taxonomy.

paymentsEnabled.description: False unless a current provider observation demonstrates enabled card payments.

payoutsEnabled.description: False unless a current provider observation demonstrates enabled payouts.

requirementsCurrent.description: False when the provider observation is absent, stale, future-dated, or has age greater than or equal to 300 seconds.

providerObservedAt.description: Provider observation Unix timestamp in seconds, or null when no provider observation exists.

url.description: Short-lived bearer URL. Do not persist, cache, or log it.

ListPaymentIntentsResponse.description: One keyset page of payment intents, ordered by `createdAt` then `id`, both descending. That pair is a total order, so paging cannot skip or repeat an intent while other intents are being created.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, absent on the last page. Replay it unchanged with the identical filters.

RefundReason.description: Caller-declared context. It never changes the economics of the refund.

RefundStatus.description: succeeded is set only after the compensating journal and the signed operation receipt are durable. pending covers every non-final provider state, including an outcome Tempera has not observed yet.

amount.description: Omit to refund the whole remaining refundable balance.

RefundReceipt.description: The signed operation receipt as persisted, rendered in this API's lowerCamel field convention. The Ed25519 signature covers the canonical evidence field map, not this serialization.

id.description: The durable REFUND payment operation that owns this refund.

journalId.description: Present once the compensating journal is durable.

nextPageToken.description: Pass as pageToken to read the next page. Absent on the last page.

idempotencyKey.description: Tenant-scoped idempotency key. An equivalent replay returns the original order; a changed replay is a conflict. It also derives the PayPal-Request-Id and invoice_id, so an interrupted create resumes on PayPal's side instead of creating a second order.

status.description: PayPal's order status at creation, e.g. CREATED or PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED. It is never settlement evidence.

expiresAt.description: PayPal's order expiration time, when PayPal supplies one.

WebhookEventType.description: A signed event type a webhook endpoint may subscribe to.

WebhookEndpointStatus.description: `disabled` endpoints keep their delivery history and receive nothing.

WebhookSigningKey.description: A platform public key a delivered event may be signed with. Verify Ed25519 over `"tempera-payments:consumer-event:v1\n" || body` against the raw request body.

url.description: Absolute HTTPS URL with no user information and no fragment. Plain HTTP is accepted for loopback hosts only.

signingKeys.description: The platform verify keys currently configured, so a delivery can be verified without a second call. All listed keys are trusted; match the delivered `tempera-event-signature` keyId.

nextPageToken.description: Absent when this is the last page.

eventId.description: The `id` of the signed event, matching the delivered `tempera-event-id` header.

lastStatusCode.description: HTTP status the receiver last answered with, when it answered.

lastErrorCode.description: Stable failure identifier, for example `WEBHOOK_HTTP_500`, `WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT`, or `ENDPOINT_DISABLED`.

nextPageToken.description: Absent when this is the last page.

externalId.description: The brand's own customer identifier. Unique per tenant when present, which is what makes creation idempotent.

metadata.description: At most 20 brand-owned string entries. Keys are 1 to 64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.-]; values are at most 255 characters and carry no control characters.
At most 20 brand-owned string entries. Keys are 1 to 64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.-]; values are at most 255 characters and carry no control characters.

providerBindings.description: Provider customers bound to this customer. Empty until the first setup session creates one.

nextPageToken.description: Present only when more customers match. Pass it back as `pageToken`.

idempotencyKey.description: Reuse this key when retrying; an identical retry replays the original session and a changed one is a conflict.

url.description: Short-lived provider-hosted bearer URL. Do not persist, cache, or log it.

PaymentMethodCard.description: The non-sensitive display fields the provider publishes. There is no field here that can carry a PAN or CVV.

nextPageToken.description: Present only when more payment methods remain. Pass it back as `pageToken`.

paymentMethodId.description: A saved payment method belonging to the customer named by the payment intent.

offSession.description: True when the shopper is not present. Defaults to true, which is what a one-click reorder is.

providerReference.description: The provider charge object this attempt created. Settlement is validated against an independent retrieval of it, never against this response.

status.description: The provider attempt outcome. `succeeded` means the provider accepted the charge; it is not a Tempera settlement, which is only produced by verified webhook reconciliation.

nextActionUrl.description: Present only for `requiresAction`. The brand completes authentication with its own provider client-side flow.
